findings.evidence: R7: "The Red lane (human-led, per `rules/non-negotiable.md` PROTECTED_PATHS_REQUIRE_RED_LANE) does not have its TDD discipline enforced by `specflow:develop` — the human leads, the skill assists on bounded subtasks. The TDD configurable knob applies only to Green; Yellow and Red are fixed."
findings.claim: Protected-path work is forcibly Red-lane under PROTECTED_PATHS_REQUIRE_RED_LANE, and R7 then removes specflow:develop TDD enforcement for that lane. That creates an explicit path where protected-path tasks skip the Red artefact requirement entirely, even when the same task would otherwise be Yellow-mandatory tests-first because of weak verifiability.
findings.proposed_change: Amend R7/AC-10 to distinguish lane control from artefact audit: Red-lane protected-path tasks remain human-led, but if the AI assists by drafting or changing testable code, the skill must either require a human-supplied Red artefact before any AI Green-like implementation assistance or record `red: skipped (human-led Red lane)` with no `green: passed` marker emitted by the skill.

findings.evidence: R9: "Each marker is one line in the manifest with this exact shape (the schema 017 owns):" ... "Schema dependency: 019-per-task-manifest is the eventual canonical home for these markers. Until 019 lands, 017 writes the three lines into a stub `## Per-task manifest stub` section appended at the bottom of `{NNN-slug}-tasks.md` per task; 019 absorbs the section when it lands by promoting the stub to its own per-task manifest file. The marker schema (the three-line block above) is owned by 017; 019 reads the schema unchanged."
findings.claim: 017 pre-claims canonical ownership over a future 019 manifest schema. If 019 lands with a structured per-task manifest format, different timestamp precision, machine-readable outcome enum, or non-line-oriented storage, 017's 'exact shape' and '019 reads unchanged' requirement will force 019 to inherit an implementation detail from an interim stub.
findings.proposed_change: Reword R9 so 017 owns only the interim stub contract and semantic fields (`red`, `green`, `refactor`, outcome, timestamp, note). State that 019 owns the canonical manifest schema and must provide a migration/adapter from the 017 stub rather than being required to read the three-line block unchanged.

findings.evidence: AC-1: "`develop/SKILL.md` Phase D body contains three subheadings — `### D.1 Red`, `### D.2 Green`, `### D.3 Refactor` (or the equivalent literal substrings `Red`, `Green`, `Refactor` under H3 markers within Phase D). Phase E and Phase F headings are unchanged in scope. (Verified via `grep -E '^### D\.[123]|^## Phase [DEF]' plugins/specflow/skills/develop/SKILL.md`.)"
findings.claim: The grep command reports matching headings but does not define an expected ordered output or fail when D.2 appears before D.1. A post-change file could contain all three subheadings out of Red -> Green -> Refactor order and still look compliant if the verifier only checks presence.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the grep-only verifier with an order assertion, for example an awk/perl check that extracts Phase D headings and fails unless the first three D subheadings are exactly `### D.1 Red`, `### D.2 Green`, `### D.3 Refactor` before `## Phase E`; include the expected output in AC-1.

findings.evidence: R8: "Extend `test/SKILL.md` `--plan-only` mode (currently at `test/SKILL.md:39, 51, 214`) so that with the additional `--task T{N}` flag it writes the per-task plan section into `{NNN-slug}-test.md` and marks the primary AC's test case as `Status: red (failing)` by default. The Green sub-phase flips the marker to `Status: green (passing)` after `vitest` (or the configured runner) confirms the implementation passes."
findings.claim: `Status: red (failing)` is a documentation marker written during `--plan-only`, not runner output. R5/AC-3 only require that the marker string exists before Green entry, so an implementation can satisfy the Red artefact contract without ever proving the test actually fails before code is written.
findings.proposed_change: Add a Red-phase verification requirement: after authoring the test and before D.2, run the targeted test against the pre-implementation state and capture the failing runner exit/output in `{NNN-slug}-test.md` or an artefact file. D.2 may flip to `Status: green (passing)` only when the same targeted test command subsequently exits 0; if the pre-implementation run passes, block as an invalid Red artefact.
